question: Step 1 on nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b, on one RTX A6000: how often do its answers depend on the batch, does the server's fixed padding freeze them, and do the places where they flip find errors better than the model's own confidence?

rules.flags: scripts/step1_places.py: precision is the flag's spans that are not right over its spans; recall is the word errors a perfect correction of every flagged span would remove, over all the side's word errors; each null draws spans of the same lengths at random, 1,000 draws, seed 20260924
rules.flips_vs_confidence: the flips are the place flag on side a, the served (fixed) answer; the confidence flag marks side a's K lowest-confidence words, K being the words the flips mark
rules.places_analysis: scripts/unstable_words.py analyse via scripts/step1_places.py, whose labels name side a 'alone' and side b 'in_batch' (or 'batch'); out-of-dictionary figures are not derived here (no word list in these records)
rules.punctuation_only: a text-divergent recording whose two transcripts agree after words()
rules.rates: over the recordings checked, rounded to 5 decimals (scripts/step1_places.py rate)
rules.served_right: the flips' spans that are right: by the flag's rule (span_not_right, a gap not right only when a reference word is missing there), spans minus not_right; by analyse's rule, which also calls a gap not right when side b's words there are right, spans minus not_right_by_analyse
rules.ticks: server.load as each capture recorded it; the tick budget is not stamped in the captures
rules.tie_range: scripts/step1_places.py tie_range: when words tie at the confidence cutoff, every choice of the tied words that fills K, scored without nulls; each figure's lowest and highest. The flag's own figures are the seeded choice's
rules.timing_only: the two texts are equal and the word timings (word, start, end) are not
rules.wer: scripts/step1_places.py corpus figures: word Levenshtein distance to the reference, summed over every checked recording, over the reference words, after its normalise(); side a and side b as the arm names them
rules.word_level: a text-divergent recording whose two transcripts differ after the probe's words() (probes/stock_divergence.py: lowercased, every run of characters other than word characters, apostrophes and spaces made a space)
